test_title: RRB ALP CBT-I 2024 Official Paper (Held On: 28 Nov, 2024 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: The Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Act, 2024 that aims to prevent unfair means in public examinations and common entrance tests held across the country, came into effect in which month of 2024?
solution:
The correct answer is __**June**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Act, 2024, aimed at preventing unfair practices in public examinations and common entrance tests across India, came into effect on **June 21, 2024**.
 
• The Act was **introduced in the Lok Sabha **on February 5, 2024, passed by both houses of Parliament by February 9, 2024, and received presidential assent on February 12, 2024.
 
• The** Act comprehensively defines "unfair means" to include:**
 
 
• **Leaking or attempting **to leak question papers or answer keys.
 
• Assisting candidates during examinations through unauthorized communication or providing solutions.
 
• Tampering with computer systems or networks related to the examination process.
 
• Impersonating or facilitating impersonation of candidates.
 
• Conducting fake examinations or issuing counterfeit documents.
 
• Altering official records to manipulate merit lists or rankings.
 
 
 
• **Penalties:****​**
 
 
• Imprisonment ranging from **three to ten years**, depending on the severity of the offence.
 
• Fines up to **₹1 crore** for organised malpractices.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__ **

 
• **Issues Related to the Public Examination Bill 2024**

 
 
• Concerns include the implementation challenges of new technologies, potential state-level resistance to a uniform framework, and ensuring the central regulatory authority functions without bias. Additionally, there are worries about the Bill's impact on the already overburdened judicial system with cases of examination malpractices.
 
• **Discretion to State Governments:** Since the said bill is of model draft nature, disparities in its implementation across states are possible. This situation can make its implementation on the ground difficult.
 
• **Creative Loopholes in Sanctions:** Provisions like fines on service providers appear to be loose, looking like an eyewash and can easily be dodged by the defaulters.
 
• **Clarity of National Technical Committee:** There is no defined guidance on what will constitute the national technical committee and what will be its mandate. This has the potential of creating a committee which might not be of much value in framing security protocols.
 
• **Stringency That Is Legally Challenged**: The stringency of measures, including non-bailability and non-compoundability, may run into a legal challenge on the basis of the principles of proportionality and adherence to the principles of natural justice.
